pr_title: net: DHCPv4: Filter NAK during requesting state
pr_body:
During the requesting state, ignore NAKs from any
non-requesting server.  This gives the requesting
server a chance to ACK the request.

fixes #50868
pr_comments:
See logs below proving the fix.

DHCP server 2 = 192.168.84.1

This does not look valid according to RFC2131:

      If the client receives a DHCPNAK message, it cannot reuse its
      remembered network address.  It must instead request a new
      address by restarting the configuration process, this time
      using the (non-abbreviated) procedure described in section
      3.1.  This action also corresponds to the client moving to
      the INIT state in the DHCP state diagram.

and

      If the network is correct, then the DHCP server should check if
      the client's notion of its IP address is correct. If not, then the
      server SHOULD send a DHCPNAK message to the client. If the DHCP
      server has no record of this client, then it MUST remain silent,
      and MAY output a warning to the network administrator. This
      behavior is necessary for peaceful coexistence of non-
      communicating DHCP servers on the same wire.

Seems like a bug in the DHCP server

Yeah, I think this solution I proposed is not exactly correct.
There is an issue with the Zephyr implementation though. I have over 70 devices on my network and the Zephyr one is the only one that has an issue an spins forever not getting an address.
I think the proper solution here is the client should keep track of the server address it is requesting for and ignore naks for other servers in the requesting state.
See Section 4.4 of the RFC. It specifically has a point where the client can choose which server to request from. Once it requests, it should only care about responses from that server, not others. If at that point it gets a nak from the server it requests to, then it should start over.

See Section 4.4 of the RFC. It specifically has a point where the client can choose which server to request from. Once it requests, it should only care about responses from that server, not others. If at that point it gets a nak from the server it requests to, then it should start over.

Sounds reasonable to me.

issue_context.title: DHCP never binds if a NAK is received during the requesting state
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
If a NAK is received during the requesting state the DHCP process starts over.
This can lead to a state where a device keeps trying DHCP forever and never succeeds.

**To Reproduce**
This was discovered when running on a network with two DHCP servers.
DHCP server 1 has slots left in its IP address range and DHCP server 2 has no slots left so it only replies with NAKs.


**Expected behavior**
Instead of starting the DHCP process over when a NAK is received, it should just ignore the NAK incase a different server responds with an ACK.

**Logs and console output**
DHCP server 1 = 192.168.210.1
DHCP server 2 = 192.168.84.1
Log showing DHCP server 2 interrupting the process even though it has no IP address slots left.
